notes: §1985:XV.3.2.4 GR3 a runs the debugging section of a procedure-name-1 subject "Immediately before each execution of the named procedure". A section subject is one trigger point at the section's first pc, named by the section (kb/Work PB5083, PB5414). A section of no paragraphs (§1985:IV.6.4.1.2) had no pc, so it was never recorded as a subject and the debugging section's DEBUG-ITEM references were emitted with no runner (CS0103 __dbgItem). Since kb/Work PB5568 landed, CollectNondeclaratives gives a zero-paragraph section the one no-op pc a declarative section already had (AddEmptyAnonymousParagraph, DEBUG-LINE the section header's line, GR12 leaves the identification to the implementor) wherever a debugging section is compiled, so AddDebugSectionSubject records it and the dispatcher fires the trigger on the PERFORM (PERFORM LOOP) and on the fall-through into it (FALL THROUGH). Probed at 85: S2 empty middle section named in USE FOR DEBUGGING ON S2: DS S2 PERFORM LOOP, AFTER PERFORM, DS S2 FALL THROUGH; the empty first section S0 as subject: DS S0 START PROGRAM then P1. The witness pb5568_debug_empty_section_subject_85 pins both.

next.reason: 1985: "When procedure-name-1 is specified in a USE FOR DEBUGGING statement that debugging section is executed"; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the Debug feature; the 2023 USE rules cover only AFTER EXCEPTION, BEFORE REPORTING and exception objects.". 2023 USE statement rules have no FOR DEBUGGING format, and no clause holds the Debug module, so the debugging-section execution rule is dropped.
